name: Kerf
notes: Fintech-style branding ('Liquidity that trades & grows', kerf.finance), Website+Twitter present. 13h old at capture, +1052% 24h, healthy liquidity/mcap ratio (~0.12). On-chain: no mint/pause/blacklist/fee-control selectors found, no owner() function at all (contract has no admin backdoor to renounce).

name: Route
notes: Clean minimal wordmark logo, Website+Twitter present. 14h old at capture, +13,708% 24h, six-figure liquidity. On-chain clean (no mint/pause/blacklist, no owner()).

name: Phera
notes: Bold neon gaming/tech wordmark, liquidity shown as locked in the UI, Website+Twitter+Telegram present. IMPORTANT CALIBRATION NOTE: was actually down -35.81% 24h at the moment of capture despite being labeled a win — a 'win' label does not mean the token was up at every point you might see it; don't treat a single negative 24h reading as disqualifying on its own. On-chain clean; 2 much-smaller same-named clone tokens exist but the real one is clearly the dominant pool by size.

name: Agent Sora
notes: Anime-character AI-agent branding — visually meme-adjacent (character art, bold color) but thematically an AI-agent narrative, not a joke name. Heavily boosted (#3 rank, 500 boosts), only 1h old at capture, +1011% 24h. CALIBRATION NOTE: on-chain re-check minutes apart showed market cap swinging wildly ($14.5K to $122K to $101K to $18K) purely from thin-pool price impact — extreme volatility can coexist with a 'win' label; don't read a single snapshot's mcap as stable. On-chain contract itself clean (no mint/pause/blacklist).

name: Port
notes: One of the few examples with an actual visible product screenshot as its header image (tryport.net mail/envelope UI mockup), not just a logo — real evidence of a built product rather than a claim. IMPORTANT CALIBRATION NOTE: was down -92.67% 24h at the moment of capture despite the win label — likely categorized as a win based on the visible real product, independent of price action at that moment. On-chain clean; a second unrelated same-named 'Port' token also exists on-chain (small, likely coincidental reuse of a common word rather than a targeted clone).

name: Assay
notes: Abstract chart-line icon (thematically fits an analysis/'assay' product name), Website+Twitter present. 35m old at capture, +570% 24h, one of the healthier liquidity/mcap ratios in this whole set (~0.15-0.45 depending on snapshot). On-chain clean; smaller same-named tokens exist elsewhere (likely coincidence, not a targeted clone of this specific pool).

name: Scarce
notes: No website link at capture (Twitter only) — weak legitimacy signal for a 1h-old token. VERIFIED ON-CHAIN: at least 5 different 'Scarce'-named tokens were deployed on Robinhood Chain within the same ~17-minute window the same day — a same-day copycat/name-squatting cluster, not a single project with a rocky chart. Negative across all timeframes at capture. Contract itself is clean (no mint/pause/blacklist) — the failure mode here is clone confusion + weak legitimacy signals, not a malicious contract.

name: Plinth
notes: STRONGEST 'looked great, still failed' example in this set: polished custom artwork and copy ('THE FLOOR ONLY GOES UP', podium imagery) — genuinely professional-looking branding, arguably the best-produced visual of any token in this whole reference set. Still -92.79% 24h. VERIFIED ON-CHAIN: at least 4 other 'Plinth'-named tokens exist, INCLUDING one using the homoglyph symbol 'PLlNTH' (lowercase L substituted for capital I) — a textbook impersonation/typosquat trick. Liquidity ($5.6K) exceeded market cap ($3.7K) at capture — an inverted ratio that usually means most of the float has already been sold into the pool. Contract itself clean (no mint/pause/blacklist): professional branding is not evidence of legitimacy.

name: homopad
notes: Clean minimal typographic branding, generic short name. Liquidity ($5.0K) exceeded market cap ($2.9K) at capture. Zero trading activity across all timeframes at capture, and re-checking the pool over a week later showed it still sitting at essentially the same tiny size — a stalled/abandoned pool with no organic demand ever materializing, not an active rug so much as a project nobody bought into. Contract clean on-chain.

name: K WHEN
notes: STRONGEST 'narrative alone isn't enough' example in this set: genuinely plausible utility copy ('Program your wallet. Non-custodial wallet automation.' with concrete feature tags — Timed Transfer, Recurring Transfer, Auto Split) that reads like a real product pitch, not buzzword spam. Failed anyway: liquidity ($6.1K) exceeded market cap ($4.4K), dead activity across all timeframes, -30.91% 24h. Contract clean on-chain (no mint/pause/blacklist) — this is a case where the utility narrative would score well on believability alone, but market execution (liquidity, actual demand) still failed.

name: Slot
notes: Highly specific, technical infra pitch ('A sovereign EVM chain. One block every second.', stated Chain ID 4242, website slot.io) — reads as a legitimate L2/appchain narrative, more specific and verifiable-sounding than most tokens seen on this chain. Liquidity, market cap and FDV were all ~$10.1K at capture AND still ~$10.1K when re-checked later — the pool never moved beyond its seed liquidity at all; zero organic buy/sell volume ever materialized. Lesson: a specific, technically-literate pitch can still attract zero real demand. Contract clean on-chain.

name: RH-VRF
notes: CLEAREST VERIFIED LIQUIDITY-DRAIN EXAMPLE in this set. Plausible crypto-infra narrative ('Verifiable randomness · Five of nine' — VRF is a real cryptographic primitive). On-chain re-checks taken minutes apart shortly after launch showed pool liquidity collapsing from $7,252 to $5.93 to $0.57 while market cap swung wildly ($6K to $58K to $17K) — a clear signature of liquidity being withdrawn, not organic trading. -90.51% 24h at capture. The token contract itself has no mint/pause/blacklist function — the risk here was liquidity-provider behavior (pulling the pool), not a malicious token contract, which is exactly the kind of thing a pure contract-bytecode check will never catch on its own.

name: HEIST
notes: Clean logo, only a website link at capture (no Twitter). VERIFIED ON-CHAIN: at least 4 other 'Heist'/'HEIST'-named tokens exist on Robinhood Chain, including one much older, larger, unrelated project (~$527K mcap from over a month earlier) and 2-3 same-day small clones — a popular/generic name gets reused by unrelated launches, making it genuinely hard for a buyer to know which 'Heist' they're looking at. -64.67% 24h at capture. Contract clean on-chain.

name: Flash AI
notes: MOST SOPHISTICATED PITCH IN THE ENTIRE SET, and it still failed: 'The Internet of Agents. Discovery, payment, and verifiable settlement — in one call.' explicitly citing the real x402 agentic-payments protocol standard, USDC, and 'Open source, MIT'. VERIFIED ON-CHAIN: 3 near-identical 'Flash AI'/FLASH tokens were deployed within the same 7-minute window the same day — near-simultaneous copycat launches racing each other for the same name. -78.29% in just 5 minutes at capture. Contract itself clean on-chain (no mint/pause/blacklist). This is the strongest evidence in the whole set that a highly technical, specifically-named, plausible-sounding infra pitch is not proof of legitimacy.

name: Vault
notes: Generic one-word name with a generic stock-style abstract water/bubble header image — no distinctive branding effort visible at all. Useful direct contrast against K WHEN / Slot / Flash AI in this set, which all put in real narrative effort and still failed just as hard — low-effort branding and high-effort branding both failed here, so branding effort alone isn't the differentiator either. Multiple unrelated tokens share similar 'Vault'-ish names on this chain ('Vault Rooms', 'PonsVault'), adding generic-name confusion on top.

name: Ascii Pons
notes: ASCII-art pixel-character logo with a 'media/asciipons.txt' tagline — a joke/novelty visual style, leaning meme-adjacent even though the name itself isn't an explicit joke. Good calibration example: visual style alone (retro ASCII/glitch art, novelty typography) can be a real signal of lower quality/meme intent even when the name doesn't scream 'meme'.

name: Vector Protocol
notes: Plausible security/privacy narrative ('Distributed decryption · All nodes contributing'). VERIFIED PUMP-AND-DUMP: capture showed +2,293% 24h alongside a simultaneous -82.76% crash in the preceding 5 minutes; re-checking later showed market cap had fallen all the way back to ~$3.4K, essentially round-tripping back to near its starting size right after the spike. Lesson: a huge 24h percentage gain on a chart can coexist with, and immediately precede, a near-total collapse — momentum alone (even triple-digit-percent momentum) is not a legitimacy signal.
